checks.prompt: A vaccine store must be held at or below `-20 °C`. Tuesday logged `-18 °C`. Is that within limit?

options.label: No, it is warmer than the limit
Yes, because 18 is a smaller number than 20
options.why: consistent with comparing the digits and ignoring the side of zero. Among negatives the larger digit is the smaller number, so `-18` lies to the right of `-20` and is warmer.

options.label: It cannot be decided from one reading
options.why: consistent with treating a single reading as insufficient evidence, but a limit is a threshold and one reading above it is already a breach.

checks.solution: `-18` lies to the right of `-20` on the line, so it is warmer. "At or below" needs a position further left, such as `-20` or `-25`.

followUp.prompt: Of the readings `-22`, `-18` and `-25`, enter the coldest.
followUp.solution: `-25` lies furthest left, so it is coldest, although `25` is the largest digit.

checks.solution: `-25` lies further left on the number line, so it is the smaller number.

responses.why: consistent with ranking by absolute value. `|-25|` exceeds `|-18|`, but the bars discard the side of zero, which is what an order comparison needs.

followUp.solution: `25 - 18 = 7`. Both bars report a distance from zero, and a distance is never negative.

checks.prompt: Evaluate `-(-22)` and explain what the outer negative sign does.
checks.solution: A minus sign in front means "the opposite of", so this asks for the opposite of negative twenty-two.

responses.why: consistent with treating one sign as a typing slip and deleting it. Each sign is an instruction.
consistent with reading the two signs as cancelling to nothing rather than as two applications of "the opposite of".

followUp.prompt: A number and its opposite always sum to the same value. Enter `-22 + 22`.
followUp.solution: Zero, which is exactly what "same distance from zero, other side" means.
